messages:
Maria V: Hey team — I opened a small docs PR that needs a quick review. It's about the Optimize toolkit: clarifies how batching + caching interact with quantization fallbacks. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4892 :wave:

Alex J: on it. do you want a python snippet or both py + ts? :thinking_face:

Maria V: both please. keep them tiny — show how to opt into a fallback model when quantized model raises a runtime shape/precision error. the current draft is a bit wordy, and the config sample confuses folks about cache key scope.

Devon R: can you paste the problematic snippet here? easier to iterate in-thread.

Maria V: pasted below. current version uses the old client.optimize call which we deprecated:

```python
# old snippet in PR
client.optimize(model="rwkv-8q", batching=True, cache_scope="global")
```

People misread "cache_scope=global" as meaning cross-tenant. need to change wording and show best practice: use per-route keys and include model-variant in the cache key. Also note fallback strategy should prefer compatible quantized variant before switching to full-precision CPU fallback due to latency tradeoffs.

Alex J: ok — propose replacement snippet like this:

```python
# recommended pattern
from redwood import RedwoodClient

c = RedwoodClient()

# create an optimize profile that prefers quantized variant but falls back gracefully
profile = {
  "model": "rwkv-8q",
  "cache_key_components": ["route_id", "model_variant", "prompt_hash"],
  "fallback_order": ["rwkv-8q", "rwkv-16q", "rwkv-fp16"],
  "batching": {"max_tokens": 256, "latency_slo_ms": 120}
}

c.optimize.apply_profile(profile)
```

Alex J: short comment: don't expose raw dict in the docs copy — show conceptual fields + link to full config reference.

Maria V: yeah, that reads better. add a one-sentence note: "Use route-scoped cache keys (route_id) to avoid cross-tenant leakage; include model_variant so cache hits are semantically correct."

Samir (docs): I'll take the PR and do wording + link fixes. Quick Q: do we want to call out SDK helper helpers like `optimize.with_fallback()` that we added last quarter? Might make snippet even shorter.

Devon R: call it out — but show both: the helper for quickstart + the explicit profile for teams that want full control. For the helper, something like:

```js
// JS helper pattern
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'

const client = new RedwoodClient()

await client.optimize.withFallback({
  model: 'rwkv-8q',
  cacheKey: (ctx) => `${ctx.routeId}:${ctx.modelVariant}:${ctx.promptHash}`,
  fallback: ['rwkv-8q','rwkv-16q','rwkv-fp16']
})
```

Lena QA: small nit — the helper currently expects `cacheKey` to return a string; docs should show a lambda example like you did. also add a note that when fallback escalates to fp16 CPU the request may breach latency SLOs; recommend setting a circuit-breaker.

Maria V: good call. add this sentence under the code block: "If a fallback target is CPU FP16, add a circuit-breaker to avoid SLO violations (see Optimize -> fallbacks guide)." and link to the fallback guide once Samir updates links.

Samir (docs): grabbing this now. I'll:
- replace the old code blocks with the two new snippets (helper + explicit profile)
- reword the cache scoping paragraph so it doesn't use the ambiguous word "global"
- add a small note about latency/circuit-breakers
- fix two dead links in the migration guide

Docs-bot: PR #4892 status: open — requested review from @Samir (docs), @Alex J. CI: docs lint OK :white_check_mark:

Alex J: I can review wording today lunchtime. one more ask: include a tiny command example showing how to run the local snippet test harness (so engineers can validate behavior end-to-end). e.g.

```bash
# run the snippet harness (local emulation)
make docs-snippet-test SNIPPET=optimize-quant-fallback
```

Maria V: perfect. Samir — if you want I can add the test harness command to the PR as a follow-up commit.

Samir (docs): please do — then I can merge after a quick pass. Thanks y'all :tada:

Maria V: thanks! :thumbsup:
